L1:# Test Strategy
L2:
L3:## 1. Objective
L4:
L5:The testing strategy for the Support Ticket Management System is designed to verify the correctness, reliability, and maintainability of the application while keeping the test suite practical and aligned with the project size.
L6:
L7:The most critical tests are those that guard business rules, backend validation, and ticket lifecycle enforcement. Special emphasis must be placed on proving that the backend rejects invalid ticket state transitions and that the initial ticket state is OPEN.
L8:
L9:## 2. Testing principles
L10:
L11:- Test real behavior, not implementation details.
L12:- Prefer small, focused tests over large, brittle test suites.
L13:- Validate behavior at the correct layer: UI, API, service, persistence, or business rule.
L14:- Keep tests readable and maintainable.
L15:- Use the backend as the source of truth for validation and state-machine enforcement.
L16:- Avoid tests that only assert framework behavior or mock behavior rather than observable application outcomes.
L17:
L18:## 3. Test scope by layer
L19:
L20:### 3.1 Unit tests
L21:
L22:Unit tests should validate isolated business logic and domain behavior.
L23:
L24:Focus areas:
L25:
L26:- Ticket validation rules
L27:- Ticket state transition validation logic
L28:- Business-rule checks for required fields and invalid transitions
L29:- Validation of priority and other constrained fields
L30:- Small helper logic, if any
L31:
L32:Examples:
L33:
L34:- Ticket title is required
L35:- Ticket description is required
L36:- Priority value is recognized and accepted
L37:- Invalid status transition is rejected
L38:
L39:### 3.2 Repository tests
L40:
L41:Repository tests verify persistence behavior and database interaction contracts.
L42:
L43:Focus areas:
L44:
L45:- Persisting a new ticket
L46:- Retrieving tickets by ID and by list query
L47:- Filtering by status
L48:- Saving comments for a given ticket
L49:- Query behavior for search and list operations
L50:- Default initial state is OPEN when a ticket is created
L51:
L52:Examples:
L53:
L54:- A created ticket is stored with status OPEN
L55:- A ticket can be retrieved by ID
L56:- Filtering by status returns only matching tickets
L57:- A comment is linked to the correct ticket
L58:
L59:### 3.3 Controller/API tests
L60:
L61:Controller tests validate the public API contract and the behavior of HTTP endpoints.
L62:
L63:Focus areas:
L64:
L65:- Create ticket endpoint
L66:- List tickets endpoint
L67:- Get ticket detail endpoint
L68:- Update ticket fields
L69:- Change status endpoint
L70:- Add comment endpoint
L71:- Search endpoint
L72:- Filter-by-status endpoint
L73:
L74:Examples:
L75:
L76:- Create ticket returns 201 and the created ticket payload
L77:- List tickets returns 200 and the correct collection
L78:- Ticket detail returns 404 for a missing ticket
L79:- Invalid status transition returns 409 Conflict
L80:- Empty or invalid request payload returns a validation error response
L81:
L82:### 3.4 Integration tests
L83:
L84:Integration tests validate that the application works correctly when multiple components interact together.
L85:
L86:Focus areas:
L87:
L88:- Full ticket creation workflow
L89:- Full ticket update workflow
L90:- End-to-end status transitions through allowed lifecycle steps
L91:- Comment creation and retrieval
L92:- Search and filter behavior across the application stack
L93:
L94:Examples:
L95:
L96:- Create a ticket, then fetch it by ID, then update it, then filter by its current status
L97:- Create a ticket with status OPEN, transition to IN_PROGRESS, then RESOLVED, then CLOSED
L98:- Create a ticket from OPEN and cancel it successfully
L99:
L100:## 4. State-machine test strategy
L101:
L102:State-machine validation is a critical requirement and must be tested thoroughly.
L103:
L104:### 4.1 Core rule
L105:
L106:The backend must reject every invalid transition, and the initial state must be OPEN.
L107:
L108:### 4.2 Required state-machine tests
L109:
L110:- A newly created ticket has status OPEN.
L111:- OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS is allowed.
L112:- IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED is allowed.
L113:- RESOLVED -> CLOSED is allowed.
L114:- OPEN -> CANCELLED is allowed.
L115:- IN_PROGRESS -> CANCELLED is allowed.
L116:
L117:State that every transition not explicitly listed as valid must be tested/rejected, not only the examples.
L118:
L119:### 4.3 Invalid transition tests
L120:
L121:The test suite must explicitly prove that the backend rejects the following invalid transitions:
L122:
L123:- CLOSED -> OPEN
L124:- RESOLVED -> OPEN
L125:- CANCELLED -> OPEN
L126:- OPEN -> RESOLVED
L127:- OPEN -> CLOSED
L128:- IN_PROGRESS -> OPEN
L129:- IN_PROGRESS -> CLOSED
L130:- RESOLVED -> IN_PROGRESS
L131:- RESOLVED -> CANCELLED
L132:- CLOSED -> IN_PROGRESS
L133:- CLOSED -> RESOLVED
L134:- CLOSED -> CANCELLED
L135:- CANCELLED -> IN_PROGRESS
L136:- CANCELLED -> RESOLVED
L137:- CANCELLED -> CLOSED
L138:
L139:### 4.4 Backend enforcement requirement
L140:
L141:The test strategy must ensure that invalid transitions are rejected by the backend before persistence occurs.
L142:
L143:This should be proven with tests that:
L144:
L145:- attempt an invalid transition through the API
L146:- verify the HTTP status is 409 Conflict
L147:- verify the ticket state remains unchanged after the failed request
L148:- verify the database still contains the original status
L149:
L150:This requirement is essential and must not be treated as optional.
L151:
L152:## 5. Backend validation tests
L153:
L154:Validation tests should cover all critical input and rule checks.
L155:
L156:Focus areas:
L157:
L158:- Missing required title
L159:- Missing required description
L160:- Blank title or description values
L161:- Invalid priority values
L162:- Invalid ticket status in update requests
L163:- Invalid comment content
L164:- Invalid query parameters for filtering and sorting
L165:- Invalid ID or malformed path parameters
L166:
L167:Examples:
L168:
L169:- A create ticket request without title is rejected
L170:- A create ticket request without description is rejected
L171:- A ticket update with an unsupported status is rejected
L172:- An invalid filter value for status is rejected
L173:- An empty comment body is rejected
L174:
L175:## 6. Frontend tests
L176:
L177:Frontend tests should validate presentation and user interaction without duplicating full backend validation logic.
L178:
L179:Focus areas:
L180:
L181:- Rendering the ticket list
L182:- Displaying empty states
L183:- Showing loading states
L184:- Showing validation errors on forms
L185:- Showing API error messages
L186:- Displaying ticket status badges and lifecycle states
L187:- Search input behavior
L188:- Status filter behavior
L189:- Ticket detail screen rendering
L190:- Successful create/update/comment/status-change workflows
L191:
L192:Examples:
L193:
L194:- Ticket list shows loading state before data arrives
L195:- Empty state appears when there are no tickets
L196:- Invalid create form fields show validation messages
L197:- API error for ticket creation is displayed to the user
L198:- Selected status filter matches the visible list results
L199:
L200:## 7. Important negative tests
L201:
L202:Negative tests are essential for confidence in this project.
L203:
L204:The following should be explicitly covered:
L205:
L206:- Invalid ticket transition is rejected
L207:- Non-existent ticket returns 404
L208:- Update request for missing ticket fails
L209:- Comment against non-existent ticket fails
L210:- Invalid search query is rejected or handled predictably
L211:- Invalid status filter value is rejected
L212:- Blank required fields are rejected
L213:- Duplicate or conflicting business operations are rejected if applicable
L214:- Terminal state cannot transition back to earlier state
L215:
L216:## 8. Database persistence tests
L217:
L218:Persistence tests ensure persisted data matches real application behavior.
L219:
L220:Focus areas:
L221:
L222:- A new ticket is stored with status OPEN
L223:- A ticket update persists the changed field values
L224:- A status update persists the new state
L225:- A comment is stored against the correct ticket
L226:- Search and filter queries return persisted records correctly
L227:- Data integrity is maintained when invalid operations are rejected
L228:
L229:Examples:
L230:
L231:- Creating a ticket persists the correct title, description, priority, and initial status
L232:- Updating the assignee persists the new assignee
L233:- Changing status persists the new state after validation
L234:- Invalid state update does not change the stored status
L235:
L236:## 9. Edge cases
L237:
L238:The test suite should include edge cases that frequently cause defects.
L239:
L240:Important edge cases:
L241:
L242:- Ticket created with empty or whitespace-only title
L243:- Ticket created with empty or whitespace-only description
L244:- Search with blank or whitespace-only keyword
L245:- Filter with an unsupported status value
L246:- Update request with no fields to change
L247:- Ticket detail request for a missing or deleted record
L248:- Transition from terminal state back to any earlier state
L249:- Attempts to create or update a ticket with invalid priority values
L250:- Attempt to add a comment with empty content
L251:- Attempt to update a ticket in a terminal state when the state machine does not allow it
L252:
L253:## 10. Recommended test matrix
L254:
L255:| Area | Priority | Goal |
L256:| --- | --- | --- |
L257:| State-machine validation | High | Prove invalid transitions are rejected by the backend |
L258:| Ticket creation validation | High | Verify required fields and initial status |
L259:| Status update API | High | Validate allowed and forbidden transitions |
L260:| Repository persistence | High | Ensure correct data writes and reads |
L261:| API error mapping | High | Verify consistent failure handling |
L262:| Search and filter behavior | Medium | Ensure list queries work correctly |
L263:| Frontend user flows | Medium | Ensure correct screens and feedback |
L264:| Edge-case validation | Medium | Prevent regressions in invalid input handling |
L265:
L266:## 11. Test execution expectations
L267:
L268:- Fast feedback is important; unit and validation tests should run quickly.
L269:- Repository and integration tests should be targeted and focused.
L270:- API tests should verify contract and error semantics, not just success flows.
L271:- State-machine tests should be treated as critical regression tests.
L272:- The initial state OPEN should be explicitly asserted in create and persistence tests.
L273:
L274:## 12. Success criteria
L275:
L276:The testing strategy is successful when:
L277:
L278:- all required ticket operations work as expected
L279:- all allowed transitions pass validation
L280:- all disallowed transitions are rejected by the backend
L281:- initial status is OPEN for every newly created ticket
L282:- validation errors are consistent and meaningful
L283:- persistence behavior is reliable and database-backed
L284:- the UI reflects the real API behavior consistently
L285:
L286:## 13. Scope note
L287:
L288:This test strategy is intentionally practical and project-appropriate for a small Support Ticket Management System. It emphasizes the most important business risks: validation, lifecycle enforcement, and persistence correctness, while keeping the suite lean and maintainable.
